acceptedAnswer.text: It is pay-per-click management, mostly Google Ads, done by MMC and sold by your agency as its own. We build and run the campaigns in your client's account; you keep the client and the report.

mainEntity.name: Do you run ads in my client's own account?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. The client owns the account and we are added as managers, so there is no lock-in.

mainEntity.name: Who pays for the ad spend?

acceptedAnswer.text: The client pays the platform directly. Our fee is separate and agreed in the scope.

mainEntity.name: How much does white-label PPC management cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on the accounts, campaigns and platforms in scope, so we price each scope in writing rather than publish one rate. The fee is separate from ad spend, invoiced in Indian rupees or US dollars, with a three-month minimum.

mainEntity.name: What does a white-label PPC report include?

acceptedAnswer.text: Spend, conversions, cost per result and what changed, with notes for your client call. It carries your branding and can be sent from your domain.

mainEntity.name: Do you also do Microsoft or Amazon Ads?

acceptedAnswer.text: Microsoft Advertising can be included. For Amazon, see our white-label ecommerce page.

mainEntity.name: Can you take over an underperforming account?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. We start with an audit of tracking and structure, then share a plan before changing spend.

mainEntity.name: Will my client know MMC is involved?

acceptedAnswer.text: Only if you choose to tell them. We sign an NDA, work under your brand, send deliverables in your format and do not contact your clients unless you ask us to.

mainEntity.name: How do we get started with white-label PPC?

acceptedAnswer.text: Share the client's account details through your agency, sign the NDA and we run an audit before changing anything.

blocks.h: How white-label PPC works in practice
paras: Campaigns run in your client's own Google Ads account, with you or MMC added as a manager. The client keeps ownership of the account, so there is no lock-in, and you keep the relationship.
We use the same method as our own Google Ads service: tracking first, then structure, then scale.
blocks.cap: A Google Ads account review for an agency client.

paras: Your client owns the Google Ads account and the billing on it. Ad spend is charged by Google to the client's own payment method, not paid through MMC.

We get access in one of two ways: linked through your agency's manager account, or added as a user directly with the access level you choose. Either way, the campaigns, history, audiences and conversion settings stay in the client's account.
If the work ends, you remove our access. Nothing needs to be rebuilt or handed back, because nothing ever left the account.

blocks.h: How a month of PPC management runs
paras: Each week we review search terms and add negatives, adjust bids and budgets against the targets in the scope, test ad copy and assets, and check the product feed for Shopping. You get a short note on what changed and why.
Each month we review structure, tracking and the plan for the next month with you, before anything reaches your client.

The monthly report covers spend, conversions, cost per result and what we changed, with notes you can put in your own words. It goes out in your format, from your domain, under your logo. See white-label reporting.

We do not publish a rate card. The fee depends on the number of accounts and campaigns, the platforms involved, how complex the account is, whether tracking or a product feed needs fixing first and how often you want reporting.
The fee is separate from ad spend, invoiced in Indian rupees or US dollars, with a minimum commitment of three months. See white-label pricing models for how to set your margin.

stages.breaks: Brand and generic searches are reported as one.
stages.why: Brand searches flatter the numbers, and the client later sees the gap.
stages.does: We keep brand, generic and competitor searches apart, so your report shows where money earns and where it does not.

stages.why: The agency blames the store, the store blames the agency, and Shopping stalls.
stages.does: We list feed issues, fix what we can in the client's account and send you a clear ask for what the client must change.

stages.breaks: Automated campaigns run on thin inputs.
stages.why: Performance Max with few assets and weak signals spends money to learn.
stages.does: Assets, signals and exclusions are set before launch, with a short note for you to give the client.

stages.why: Ads that get watched but are not followed up make video look like a cost.
stages.does: Video audiences feed search and remarketing, and the report shows where they went.

stages.breaks: The report shows conversions, not profit.
stages.why: Reported conversions can sit far from what the client keeps after costs.
stages.does: We set up tracking so reports can be read against the client's margin or cost per qualified lead.
